name: agent-index-cutover
description: Tier-P F1 cutover-resilience scenario: install + provision agent-index on a fresh box, then drive the installer's real `agent-index deploy` seam (the OS-agnostic zdd active/passive graceful cutover) through a battery of THORNY situations and assert the binding invariant of the correct-install-flows effort (dotfiles#1393) -- a version cutover must NEVER kill in-flight, non-resumable work. agent-index's durable unit is the SQLite indexing queue ($AGENT_INDEX_HOME/data/tasks.db). Checks: (survive-queued-batch) a queued index task survives the cutover -- routing flips, the old service is retired, the new service is healthy, and the task row is still present in the shared durable tasks.db (re-adoption via the durable queue); (drain-gate) /drain closes the service to new work (/health -> draining, /reindex refused) and the cutover then yields a FRESH non-draining service that accepts work again; (breadcrumb-recover) an aborted cutover that strands a DRAINED survivor is healed by recovery (deploy --recover undrains it). The heavy embedding engine (separate unit, fixed port 8421) is left untouched by a service cutover and is not exercised. The probe is dependency-light (enqueues straight into the pure-SQLite TaskStore, so it needs neither torch nor lancedb) and portable stdlib-only, so it is verifiable off-Docker too. Name-free / public.
